title: Quality management
examples: What is the difference between checking and making sure something is good?
Can you explain what TQM means in a business?
How does a business use quality management?

explain.say: Today we will learn about making sure things are of high quality.
Quality control checks the final product for flaws.
Quality assurance focuses on the process to prevent errors.
Total Quality Management involves everyone in the company.
A car manufacturer uses TQM to improve engine design.
When a restaurant gets complaints, they use TQM to fix the kitchen process.

faq.q: What is the main difference between quality control and assurance?
faq.a: Quality control checks the final item to see if it is faulty. Quality assurance, however, looks at the steps taken to make it, aiming to stop faults before they happen.
asks: Does QC check the product or the method?
What is the difference between checking and preventing errors?

faq.q: Does TQM mean that only the quality manager is responsible?
faq.a: No, TQM means that every single employee, from the boss to the newest worker, must be involved in keeping quality high. It is a company-wide effort.
asks: Is TQM just a department's job?
Who has to care about quality in TQM?

faq.q: If a product fails quality control, what should happen next?
faq.a: The company should use that failure to improve its process, which is the core idea of quality assurance. They must find out why it failed.
asks: What is the next step after finding a defect?
How does failure help quality management?

faq.q: Is TQM only for big companies?
faq.a: No, TQM principles can be used by any size of organization, even small local shops. The focus is always on the customer.

faq.q: What is the main goal of quality management?
faq.a: The main goal is to consistently meet or exceed what the customer expects from the product or service. It is about trust.
asks: Why do businesses care so much about quality?
What is the ultimate aim of quality efforts?

facts: Quality Control involves inspecting goods after they are made.
Quality Assurance involves establishing procedures to prevent errors.
TQM requires commitment from every employee in the organization.
The customer's needs are the central focus of Total Quality Management.

quiz.say: A bakery owner counts the number of loaves baked each morning to ensure they meet orders.
quiz.why: This is checking the final count of items after they are made.

wrong.0: This is about checking the process, like how the dough was mixed.
wrong.1: TQM is too broad; it involves many areas, not just counting.
wrong.2: This is a tool, not the action of checking the final count.

quiz.say: A software company trains all its staff on new coding standards to reduce bugs before testing.
quiz.why: They are improving the process itself to stop bugs from happening.

wrong.1: QC would mean running the code and finding the bugs later.
wrong.2: This is input, not the internal action of training staff.
wrong.3: While part of TQM, this specific action is assurance.

quiz.say: A company redesigns its entire supply chain to use only sustainable and reliable parts.
quiz.why: This shows improvement across all parts of the business, which is TQM.

wrong.1: This is a massive change to the system, not just checking the final part.
wrong.2: While it improves the process, TQM describes the overall philosophy needed for this big change.
wrong.3: Inspection is a small part of the overall management strategy.
